tone_statements.citation: Ōtake Masami (大竹昌巳). 2024. 契丹語の音調 [Pitch Realization in Khitan]. 言語研究 (Gengo Kenkyu: Journal of the Linguistic Society of Japan) 165: 85-110. DOI 10.11435/gengo.165.0_85
tone_statements.quote: したがってこのことは，遼代初期の契丹語が，初頭音節のピッチが低く，末音節のピッチが高いという一定の音調形式を有したことを意味していると解釈することができる。... 契丹語音訳語彙の陰陽調字の分布は，この言語が左端を L 音調で明示し，緩やかなピッチの上昇ののち右端を H 音調で明示するという，左右両端の 2 つの境界画定機能をもつ音調によって形づくられるピッチ曲線を有したことを示すと解釈できる。
tone_statements.translation: This can therefore be interpreted to mean that the Khitan of the early Liao period had a fixed pitch pattern in which the pitch of the initial syllable was low and the pitch of the final syllable was high. ... The distribution of yin-register and yang-register characters in the Chinese transcriptions of Khitan words can be interpreted as showing that this language had a pitch contour shaped by two boundary-demarcating tones at its left and right edges: an L tone explicitly marking the left edge and, after a gradual rise in pitch, an H tone explicitly marking the right edge.
tone_statements.locator: p. 105 (sec. 4.1) and p. 106 (sec. 4.2); English abstract p. 110 states the same ('Khitan was a phrase language with an L tone at the left edge and an H tone at the right edge of every word or phrase')
tone_statements.summary: No lexical tone: phrase language of the Mongolic type; every word/phrase realised L at the left edge with a gradual rise to H at the right edge (initial syllable lowest, final syllable highest); reconstructed from tonal-category preferences in Liao-Chinese transcriptions.

sources.citation: 武内康則 (Takeuchi Yasunori). 2023. 契丹小字で表記された漢語音と契丹語の音韻 = Chinese loanwords transcribed in Khitan small script: an exploration of Khitan phonology. 神戸市外国語大学研究叢書 (Kobe City University of Foreign Studies monograph series) 66. Kobe: 神戸市外国語大学外国学研究所. pp. 1-312 (issued 2023-12-20)
sources.tag: read: notes on tone
sources.note: No statement on Khitan tone or accent; reports after Shen 2012 that Chinese departing-tone loan syllables were spelled with doubled vowel graphs, then sets Chinese tone aside. 5 loan spellings in (9).

tone.quote: 沈(2012)は、契丹小字で表記された漢語音に関して、去声字の表記に特徴が見られることを指摘している。(9)に示すように、去声字(全濁上声字等含む)は、主母音あるいは末尾音が重ねて表記される57。... 57 沈(2012: 48)は、安然による『悉曇蔵』に見られる声調に関する記載を元に、去声字の声調が契丹語話者には 2 音節あるいは 1 音節を超えるように感じられたため文字を増やして表記した可能性を指摘している。... ただし、これらの去声特有の表記は常に見られるものではなく、これによって韻母の表記に用いられる文字素が大きく変わるわけでもない。したがって、本研究では韻母の表記を検討する際には声調(平声、上声、去声)の違いは捨象する。
tone.locator: §4.1 契丹小字による韻母の表記, pp. 53-54 with fn. 57
tone.translation: Shen (2012) points out that, in Chinese sounds written in Khitan Small Script, the spelling of departing-tone characters shows a peculiarity. As shown in (9), departing-tone characters (including voiced-obstruent rising-tone characters etc.) have their main vowel or final sound written twice.57 ... 57 Shen (2012: 48), on the basis of the account of the tones in Annen's Shittanzō, suggests that the tone of departing-tone characters may have felt to Khitan speakers like two syllables, or more than one syllable, so that they added graphs in writing them. ... However, these spellings peculiar to the departing tone are not always found, and they do not greatly change the graphemes used to write the finals. Therefore, in this study the differences of tone (level, rising, departing) are disregarded when examining the spelling of finals.
tone.summary: No statement on Khitan tone or accent; reports after Shen 2012 that Chinese departing-tone loan syllables were spelled with doubled vowel graphs, then sets Chinese tone aside. 5 loan spellings in (9).
tone.says: No statement on Khitan tone or accent; reports after Shen 2012 that Chinese departing-tone loan syllables were spelled with doubled vowel graphs, then sets Chinese tone aside. 5 loan spellings in (9).

tone.quote: 第5節は遼代漢語の声調について論じる。...遼代漢語音の調類と調値が可能な限り推定されている。その知見に基づいて論者はさらに、契丹語の漢字音写において漢語去声字が契丹語重母音の音写に充てられる顕著な傾向が存在すること、また漢語陽調字が契丹語の初頭音節の音写に、陰調字が最終音節の音写に充てられる顕著な傾向が存在することを発見している。そして、そうした音写の様態に基づいて契丹語の音調パターンが推定されている。
tone.locator: 論文内容の要旨, summary of ch. 5 §5 (遼代漢語の声調) abstract (unpaginated)
tone.translation: Section 5 discusses the tones of Liao-period Chinese. ... the tone categories and tone values of Liao Chinese are estimated as far as possible. On that basis the author further discovers that in Chinese-character transcriptions of Khitan there is a marked tendency for Chinese departing-tone characters to be used for Khitan diphthongs, and a marked tendency for Chinese yang-register characters to be used for the initial syllable of Khitan words and yin-register characters for the final syllable. From this manner of transcription the pitch pattern of Khitan is inferred.
tone.summary: Thesis claims a Khitan word pitch pattern reconstructed from which Chinese tone-register characters transcribe initial vs final syllables; the pattern itself is not stated here.
tone.says: Thesis claims a Khitan word pitch pattern reconstructed from which Chinese tone-register characters transcribe initial vs final syllables; the pattern itself is not stated here.

sources.citation: 大竹昌巳 (Ōtake Masami). 2015. 契丹小字文献における母音の長さの書き分け [The Orthographic Distinction of Vowel Length in the Khitan Small Script]. 言語研究 (Gengo Kenkyu) 148: 81-102. DOI 10.11435/gengo.148.0_81
sources.tag: read: notes on tone
sources.note: Vowel-length spelling in Khitan Small Script; nothing on Khitan tone. Only tone content: optional doubled-vowel spelling of Chinese departing-tone loan syllables (after Shen 2012), Tables 8, 12.

tone.quote: なお，V 型字素は 1 つで長母音を表すので，同一の V 型字素が連綴されることは原則としてないが，漢語去声字の特殊表記はその例外である（表 8）。この表記は，漢語の去声字を表記する際に主母音またはコーダの半母音と一致する V 型字素を重複させて綴る（沈鍾偉 2012）というものだが，漢語去声字が常に重複形で綴られるわけではなく，あくまでも随意的な特殊表記であって，V 型字素 1 つで長母音を表すことを否定する根拠となるようなものではない 19。
tone.locator: p. 89, sec. 2.1.2 'V 型字素の分布特徴', last paragraph
tone.translation: Since one V-type grapheme by itself represents a long vowel, the same V-type grapheme is in principle never written twice in succession, but the special spelling of Chinese departing-tone (qusheng) characters is an exception (Table 8). In this spelling, when a Chinese qusheng character is written, the V-type grapheme matching the main vowel or the coda glide is doubled (Shen Zhongwei 2012); however, Chinese qusheng characters are not always spelled with the doubled form, it is merely an optional special spelling, and it gives no grounds to deny that a single V-type grapheme represents a long vowel.
tone.summary: Vowel-length spelling in Khitan Small Script; nothing on Khitan tone. Only tone content: optional doubled-vowel spelling of Chinese departing-tone loan syllables (after Shen 2012), Tables 8, 12.
tone.says: Vowel-length spelling in Khitan Small Script; nothing on Khitan tone. Only tone content: optional doubled-vowel spelling of Chinese departing-tone loan syllables (after Shen 2012), Tables 8, 12.
